title: an interactive project switcher on Work
notes: The three case-study cards became a real switcher: click a project on the left, its stage strip, statement, and details update on the right. Zero JavaScript — driven entirely by hidden radio inputs and CSS :has(), the same technique already used for hover states elsewhere on the site. Each project now carries a short stage strip (SCREEN → GENERATE → REVIEW → SHIP for the Career Operating System, matching its real pipeline; similar honest summaries for Bosch and Club House). Full case studies stay on their own pages — this is a richer preview, not a replacement.

title: a module grid on Home
notes: Inspired by a reference site Sahil pointed to: Home's lower half is now six numbered, clickable modules (Work, How I work, About, CV, Notes, and this changelog) instead of a linear stack of paragraphs — same content, restructured as real destinations. Reused the sliding-accent-bar hover already built for the Work index rather than inventing a new pattern. Footer now credits the typefaces (Newsreader & Geist Mono), a small detail borrowed from the same reference. What stayed out on purpose: the reference site's personal-data modules (cycling stats, reading list, now-playing) — copying the pattern without content only Sahil has would mean inventing facts about him.

title: atmosphere
notes: A soft, slowly-drifting glow behind Home's hero — the 'engineer's notebook' concept finally has real texture: a subtle dot-grid runs sitewide (paper, not screen). Bigger, tighter, more confident headlines everywhere, not just Home. Pull-quotes in the case studies now break wider than the text column and read louder. Cards and stat tiles lift with a soft accent-tinted glow on hover instead of just a border-color change. Still no flat gradient fills, no cursor effects, no particle backgrounds — those stay a deliberate line, not an oversight.

title: the site gets some motion
notes: A scroll-progress bar and a fade-rise reveal on scroll, both sitewide — the reveal was actually specced back when the interaction system was designed and never got built until now. Richer hover states on the Work cards, the About timeline, and How I work's principles (a sliding accent bar, not just a border-color swap). Home's tagline set larger and tighter. All of it respects prefers-reduced-motion and stays inside the CI performance budget.

title: a real CV, finally
notes: A working /cv/ page — print or save as PDF, sourced only from the same facts already vetted for About (no separate, drifting copy of the truth). Linked from the header on every page, from Home, and from About, where the old 'coming shortly' placeholder is gone.

title: a heads-up for CV traffic
notes: The URL is now on Sahil's actual CV, so real visitors land here directly — noindex only stops search engines, not a direct link. Home now opens with a small work-in-progress badge before anything else.

title: all three case studies, live
notes: Bosch and Club House join the Career Operating System. Both drafts went through a real critique pass (ChatGPT, consulted deliberately) before shipping — some of it applied (an owned-vs-supported breakdown for Bosch, concrete nouns over vague ones, a tighter verify-this checklist), some of it rejected on the record (invented resistance anecdotes, a fabricated weekly timeline, and — most importantly — a rewrite of both retrospectives, which stayed exactly as originally said, verbatim). Work index now lists all three properly instead of a queue.

title: the flagship case study
notes: The Career Operating System, live: the real pipeline as a diagram, the three design decisions as expandable asides, and a living dashboard built from the actual application tracker — target-track share, ATS match band, gate pass rate. Digital diagram for now; the hand-drawn one replaces it. Interview/offer conversion is honestly labeled 'collecting since June 2026' because that's what the data supports.

title: some actual personality
notes: The site read like a spec sheet — fair complaint. Home's boxy credentials card is now a real paragraph about who this is, with a working example of the changelog conceit right on the page (expand 'What's changed recently'). About and How I work get a couple of honest asides where the numbers alone were carrying too much of the story. A 404 page exists now too.

title: the site has a background now
notes: Real navigation across the whole site. About: the full timeline from KEIHIN through Bosch to the Career Operating System, languages, the shelf, and how to reach me. How I work: five operating principles, each with its story and evidence. Work and Notes are honest queues, not dead links — the case studies and articles land as their own increments.

title: the first real Home page
notes: Replaced the holding page with real content: the evidence-earning tagline, the Currently/work-authorization/languages block, and a temporary monogram avatar standing in until a clean portrait photo is ready. Home only for now — the case study, How I work, and About still need assets (the diagram, colleague quotes) before they're honest to build.

title: the site goes bilingual
notes: German routing at /de/, starting with Home — English-first, German follows page by page as each page is written (ADR-004). AI-drafted, human-reviewed; each German page says so, plainly, on the page.

title: dark and light, on request
notes: Manual theme toggle in the header — defaults to the visitor's OS preference, overridable and persisted, no flash on load. No new dependency: pure CSS attribute overrides plus a script under 1KB.

title: components & compliance
notes: First interaction components — disclosure block and stat tiles with definition flyouts, both zero JavaScript on native elements. Draft Impressum and Datenschutz pages (awaiting a final address). Internal lab page for component review.

title: three voices
notes: Typography decided from the specimen: Newsreader for display, the system sans for body, Geist Mono for data — self-hosted, OFL. The specimen page is retired; its verdict lives in ADR-003.

title: type & rhythm
notes: Type specimen with candidate faces for the three voices, changelog page, header and footer, CI quality gates. The site can now fail its own build for being slow.

title: foundation
notes: Astro scaffold, design tokens, GitHub Pages pipeline, ADRs 001–002, runbook, holding page. Deployed noindex — it launches when it meets its definition of done, not a date.
